mainTopic: The end of the story of the תלמיד who died young (the danger of closeness during נדה), and the opening of the משנה about the eighteen גזירות made in the attic of חנניה בן חזקיה בן גרון
overview: This amud begins at the end of a story from תנא דבי אליהו. A young תלמיד חכם died young, and אליהו explained that he was punished for being physically close to his wife during her ימי ליבון, which breaks 'לא תקרב'. רב דימי and the scholars of ארץ ישראל give milder versions of what he did, but he was punished in every version. A new משנה then says that in the attic of חנניה בן חזקיה בן גרון, בית שמאי outnumbered בית הלל and eighteen גזירות were made. אביי asks whether the משנה says 'ואלו' or 'אלו', and a ברייתא proves it is 'ואלו', so the earlier lamplight rules are among those גזירות. The גמרא praises חנניה בן חזקיה twice: his group wrote מגילת תענית, and he saved ספר יחזקאל by explaining its difficult passages. Along the way, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל explains why later generations do not record their rescues. Finally, the גמרא starts listing the eighteen גזירות with the משנה of things that disqualify תרומה, and it begins asking which תנא holds that eating impure food only disqualifies. That question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The widow asks why her learned husband died young
steps.stepSummary: The widow of the תלמיד complains: he learned and served תלמידי חכמים a great deal, so why did he die at half his days? No one could answer her.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...and he served Torah scholars a great deal. Why did he die at half his days?' And no one could give her any answer.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a story. A widow is asking a painful question: why did her husband, a great Torah learner, die so young? This sets up the investigation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her question rests on the Torah's promise that Torah brings long life ('כי הוא חייך ואורך ימיך'). His early death seems to contradict that promise. The silence of everyone around her shows how hard the question was.

keyTerms.meaning: Served Torah scholars, meaning he learned closely from them by attending them
At half his days, meaning he died young

phrases.english: and he served Torah scholars a great deal,
phrases.notes: The earlier part of the story (on the previous lines) said he learned Torah and משנה a great deal.

phrases.english: why did he die at half his days?
phrases.notes: The widow's complaint, as she goes around to the בתי מדרשות.

phrases.english: And no person would answer her anything.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of the תלמיד from תנא דבי אליהו, begun on the previous amud.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did a man full of Torah die young, when Torah promises long life?

steps.title: אליהו questions the widow about how her husband acted
steps.stepSummary: אליהו stays as her guest and asks how her husband behaved during her days of נדה and during her ימי ליבון. In the second period, she says, he was physically close to her but had no intention of relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: אליהו said: Once I was a guest at her house, and she was telling the whole story. I asked her: My daughter, during your days of נדה, how did he act toward you? She said: Heaven forbid! He did not touch me even with his little finger. I asked: During your ימי ליבון (the clean days you were counting), how did he act toward you? She said: He ate with me, drank with me, and slept with me with bodily contact, but he never thought of anything more.
steps.whatsHappening: אליהו is gathering facts by asking the widow two questions. This sets up his answer to her question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the actual bleeding days the husband was very careful. But during the seven clean days he treated her as if she were already permitted. Bodily closeness without any intention of relations is still the key detail that leads to the verdict.

keyTerms.meaning: The days of actual menstrual bleeding
The 'white' days, the seven clean days counted after bleeding stops, when she wears white garments to check

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the woman was 'pure' during ימי ליבון. Until she counts seven clean days and goes to the מקוה, she is fully a נדה in הלכה. The husband's mistake was treating this period as less strict.

phrases.english: One time I was a guest at her house
and she was relating that entire event.
And I said to her: My daughter,
during your days of menstruation, how was he with you?
She said to me: Heaven forbid,
he did not touch me even with his little finger.
During your white (clean-counting) days, how was he with you?
He ate with me and drank with me
and slept with me with bodily contact,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא עָלְתָה דַּעְתּוֹ עַל דָּבָר אַחֵר.
phrases.english: but his mind did not turn to anything else (relations).

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַרְתִּי לָהּ: בִּתִּי, בִּימֵי נִדּוּתֵךְ מַה הוּא אֶצְלֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: אליהו investigates in order to answer the widow's question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How did the husband behave during each stage of her נדה period?

steps.title: אליהו's verdict: he died for treating the clean days lightly
steps.stepSummary: אליהו tells her: Blessed is the Omnipresent who killed him, since he did not respect the Torah, which says 'Do not come near a woman in her נדה impurity.'
steps.simpleTranslation: I said to her: Blessed is the Omnipresent who killed him, because he showed no respect to the Torah. For the Torah said: 'And to a woman in the separation of her impurity you shall not come near.'
steps.whatsHappening: אליהו answers the widow's question. Her husband died because he came close to her while she was still a נדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'לא תקרב', do not come near. That word covers closeness, not only relations. So the promise of long life for Torah did not cover him, because he broke this prohibition. Torah learning does not grant special leniency.

keyTerms.meaning: Blessed is the Omnipresent (a name of השם)
Showed respect / gave honor to the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: The prohibition of 'לא תקרב' applies during the whole time a woman is a נדה, including the seven clean days. Even closeness with no intention of relations is dangerous and forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This story supports the earlier משנה that a זב should not eat with a זבה, a גזירה made out of fear that closeness will lead to sin. It also teaches that the ימי ליבון are as strict as the days of bleeding.

phrases.english: And I said to her: Blessed is the Omnipresent who killed him,
for he did not show respect to the Torah.
For the Torah said:
'And to a woman in the separation of her impurity you shall not come near.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the facts from step 2 to answer the question from step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He died because he was physically close to his wife during her ימי ליבון, which breaks 'לא תקרב'.

steps.title: רב דימי: they only shared one bed
steps.stepSummary: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל, he reported that the story was not about bodily contact. They only slept in one bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: It was one bed (they slept in the same bed, without contact).
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי gives a milder version of what the תלמיד did. In his version there was no contact at all, only sharing one bed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the sin was smaller, yet he was still punished. That makes the lesson stronger: even sharing a bed with no touching is forbidden during the נדה period.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
It was one bed.
phrases.notes: That is, there was no bodily contact. They only shared a bed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a softer version of the facts in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תלמיד only shared one bed with his wife, without bodily contact, and he was still punished.

steps.title: In ארץ ישראל: a garment separated between them
steps.stepSummary: In ארץ ישראל they say in the name of רב יצחק בר יוסף that a סינר (an apron-like garment) separated between the husband and wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the West (ארץ ישראל) they say: רב יצחק בר יוסף said, a סינר (a garment worn from the waist down) separated between him and her.
steps.whatsHappening: A third version of the story is given. They shared a bed, but a garment separated them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version adds a protective barrier, and he was still punished. The point is that no safeguard makes closeness permitted during the נדה period.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל
An apron or belt-garment worn from the waist down

steps.whatToRemember: All three versions agree that he was punished. Each softer version makes the prohibition of closeness during נדה look even stricter.

phrases.english: In the West they say:
Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef said,
a belt-garment separated between him and her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another softer version alongside רב דימי's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even with a separating garment in a shared bed, the תלמיד was punished.

steps.title: The משנה: eighteen גזירות in the attic of חנניה בן חזקיה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says these are among the הלכות said in the attic of חנניה בן חזקיה בן גרון. When the sages were counted, בית שמאי outnumbered בית הלל, and eighteen גזירות were made that day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And these are among the הלכות that the sages said in the attic of חנניה בן חזקיה בן גרון, when they went up to visit him. They took a count, בית שמאי outnumbered בית הלל, and on that day they decreed eighteen things.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes a famous gathering where a vote was taken, and the majority (בית שמאי) passed eighteen גזירות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the הלכה follows בית הלל. Here בית שמאי won because they had more people present when the vote was taken. The word 'ואלו' ('and these') starts the משנה, and the גמרא will ask what it refers to.

keyTerms.meaning: They were counted, meaning they took a vote

steps.whyThisMatters: The 'eighteen matters' are a central event in הלכה. They are a rare case where the ruling follows בית שמאי, and the rest of the sugya tries to identify them.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: And these are among the halachot that they said

phrases.aramaic: בַּעֲלִיַּית חֲנַנְיָה בֶּן חִזְקִיָּה בֶּן גָּרוֹן.
phrases.english: in the upper story of Chananya ben Chizkiya ben Garon.
When they went up to visit him, they were counted,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבּוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי עַל בֵּית הִלֵּל.
phrases.english: and Beit Shammai outnumbered Beit Hillel.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוֹנָה עָשָׂר דְּבָרִים גָּזְרוּ בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם.
phrases.english: And they decreed eighteen matters on that day.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵלּוּ מִן הַהֲלָכוֹת שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּעֲלִיַּית חֲנַנְיָה בֶּן חִזְקִיָּה בֶּן גָּרוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. The story about נדה is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the attic of חנניה בן חזקיה, בית שמאי had the majority, and eighteen גזירות were passed.

steps.title: אביי asks: does 'ואלו' point back or forward?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף whether the משנה reads 'אלו' or 'ואלו'. If it reads 'ואלו', it refers to the rules already taught. If it reads 'אלו', it refers to rules still to come.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: Did we learn 'these' or 'and these'? If we learned 'and these', it means the rules we already said. Or did we learn 'these', meaning the rules we are about to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a question about the exact wording of the משנה. The answer will decide which rules belong to the eighteen גזירות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra letter ו ('and') connects the line to what came before. With the ו, the earlier rules (such as not reading by lamplight on שבת) are part of the attic גזירות. Without it, only the rules listed later count.

keyTerms.meaning: That we are going to say below

steps.confusionAlert: This question is not just about spelling. One letter ו decides whether the earlier rules in the perek are included among the eighteen גזירות.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַב יוֹסֵף:
phrases.english: GEMARA: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
Did we learn 'these', or did we learn 'and these'?
If we learned 'and these', it means those we already said.
Or did we learn 'these', meaning those we will say below?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the opening word of the משנה in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the משנה say 'ואלו', referring back to earlier rules, or 'אלו', referring forward to later rules?

steps.title: Proof from a ברייתא that links the lamplight rules to the attic
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the rules about not delousing or reading by lamplight, and then says 'and these are among the הלכות said in the attic of חנניה'. This shows the earlier rules are included.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One may not shake out clothing (to remove lice) by the light of a lamp, and one may not read by the light of a lamp. And these are among the הלכות that they said in the attic of חנניה בן חזקיה בן גרון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to answer אביי's question. The ברייתא connects the earlier lamp rules directly to the attic gathering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rules about not delousing or reading by lamplight appear in the previous משנה. The ברייתא lists them and then says 'ואלו מן ההלכות', so those earlier rules were part of the attic גזירות.

keyTerms.meaning: Shake or check garments to remove lice
By the light of a lamp, a concern that one might tilt the lamp on שבת

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One may not delouse garments by the light of the lamp
and one may not read by the light of the lamp,
and these are among the halachot that they said

phrases.aramaic: בַּעֲלִיַּית חֲנַנְיָה בֶּן חִזְקִיָּה בֶּן גָּרוֹן.
phrases.english: in the upper story of Chananya ben Chizkiya ben Garon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer the question in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה reads 'ואלו', referring back to the earlier rules
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that places the lamplight rules right before 'ואלו מן ההלכות שאמרו בעליית חנניה'

steps.title: Conclusion: the משנה says 'ואלו'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the correct reading is 'ואלו'. The earlier rules are part of the attic גזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: we learned 'and these'. Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the question. The answer is 'ואלו', so the rules taught earlier are included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in step 8 is accepted without challenge. The earlier rules, such as not reading by lamplight, are now counted among the eighteen גזירות.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it, a formula that closes a proof

steps.whatToRemember: 'ואלו' connects back. The rules taught earlier in the perek, like not reading by lamplight on שבת, were among the eighteen גזירות from the attic of חנניה.

phrases.english: Conclude from it: we learned 'and these'. Conclude from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof from step 8 and closes the question.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה reads 'ואלו', so the earlier rules belong to the attic גזירות.

steps.title: חנניה בן חזקיה and his group wrote מגילת תענית
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that חנניה בן חזקיה and his group wrote מגילת תענית, because they cherished the memory of the troubles Israel had been saved from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Who wrote מגילת תענית? They said: חנניה בן חזקיה and his group, who held dear the troubles (and the salvations from them).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with background about חנניה בן חזקיה, the host named in the משנה. This begins a new topic about him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מגילת תענית is a list of days on which miracles happened, when fasting is not allowed. חנניה's group 'cherished the troubles', meaning they treasured the memory of each rescue enough to record it.

keyTerms.meaning: A scroll listing days of salvation when fasting is forbidden
Holding dear the troubles, meaning cherishing the memory of salvation from them

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Who wrote Megillat Taanit?
They said: Chananya ben Chizkiya and his group,
who held dear the troubles.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִי כָּתַב מְגִילַּת תַּעֲנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives background about חנניה בן חזקיה, the host named in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מגילת תענית was written by חנניה בן חזקיה and his group, because they cherished the memory of Israel's salvations.

steps.title: We also cherish the rescues, but there are too many to write
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says his generation also values the memory of the troubles Israel was saved from. They cannot write them all down because there are simply too many.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: We also hold dear the memory of the troubles. But what can we do? If we tried to write them all, we would never manage to finish.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל responds to the praise of חנניה's group for writing מגילת תענית. He explains why later generations did not add their own rescues to the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think later generations care less about their rescues because they wrote no new list. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the opposite is true. The troubles became so many that writing each one down would be impossible.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
We too hold dear the troubles (we were saved from),
but what can we do?
For if we came to write (them all),
we would not manage (to finish).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: אַף אָנוּ מְחַבְּבִין אֶת הַצָּרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the ברייתא's praise of חנניה's group for writing מגילת תענית
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Later generations do not record every rescue because there are too many to record.

steps.title: A second reason: a person who has lost his mind does not feel the hurt
steps.stepSummary: A second explanation for why we do not record our rescues: we are like a שוטה, who does not feel his own pain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: a crazy person does not feel hurt.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a different reason why later generations do not write up their rescues. We have become like a שוטה who does not notice the harm done to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reason was that there are too many troubles to count. This reason is about how we experience them. We are so used to suffering that we no longer fully feel it, so we do not think to commemorate the rescues.

keyTerms.meaning: a person who is not mentally competent

phrases.english: Alternatively: a crazy person is not hurt (he does not feel it).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, different reason for the same fact as step 11
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Like a שוטה, we no longer feel our troubles, so we do not commemorate the rescues.

steps.title: A third reason: dead flesh does not feel the scalpel
steps.stepSummary: A third explanation: just as dead flesh does not feel a scalpel cutting it, we have become numb to our troubles.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: the flesh of a dead person does not feel the scalpel.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a third comparison for why we do not record our rescues. We are like dead flesh, which feels nothing when it is cut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This image makes the numbness even stronger than the שוטה comparison. Our suffering has gone so deep that we are like something lifeless. The גמרא is about to challenge this exact comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: the flesh of a dead person

phrases.english: Alternatively:
the flesh of a dead person does not feel the scalpel.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: אֵין בְּשַׂר הַמֵּת מַרְגִּישׁ בָּאִיזְמֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third alternative reason, parallel to step 12
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We are numb to our troubles, like dead flesh that does not feel the scalpel.

steps.title: Challenge: the dead do feel pain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the scalpel comparison. רב יצחק teaches from a פסוק in איוב that maggots hurt the dead as much as a needle hurts the living.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב יצחק said: a maggot is as painful to the dead as a needle in living flesh, as it says: 'But his flesh shall hurt him, and his soul mourns over him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks step 13. If the dead really feel pain, the claim that dead flesh feels nothing cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 assumed a dead body feels nothing. רב יצחק, using a פסוק, says a dead body does feel pain from maggots. The two statements seem to contradict each other directly.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? (a formula that opens a challenge)

phrases.english: Is that so? But didn't Rav Yitzchak say:
A maggot is as painful to the dead
as a needle in living flesh,
as it is stated:
"But his flesh shall hurt him,
and his soul mourns over him" (איוב 14:22)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim made in step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that dead flesh does not feel the scalpel
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יצחק proves from a פסוק that the dead feel the pain of maggots, so dead flesh is not numb.

steps.title: Answer: it means numb, dead flesh on a living person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the comparison. It refers to dead, numb flesh on a living body, and that flesh truly does not feel the scalpel.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: the dead flesh that is on a living person does not feel the scalpel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by adjusting how we read the phrase. It is not talking about a corpse at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Dead flesh" here means numb tissue on a living person, such as an area a surgeon cuts away. That tissue really feels nothing. The comparison to our numbness still works, and it no longer conflicts with רב יצחק, who was speaking about an actual dead body.

keyTerms.meaning: that is on a living person

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא rejected the comparison. It kept the comparison and only clarified that "dead flesh" means numb tissue on a living person, not a corpse.

phrases.english: Say instead:
The dead flesh that is on a living person
does not feel the scalpel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: אֵין בָּשָׂר הַמֵּת שֶׁבַּחַי מַרְגִּישׁ בָּאִיזְמֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge raised in step 14
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed "dead flesh" meant a corpse, which רב יצחק says does feel pain.
steps.terutzMaskana: "Dead flesh" means numb tissue on a living body, which truly feels nothing.

steps.title: חנניה בן חזקיה saved ספר יחזקאל
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב praises חנניה בן חזקיה. Without him, ספר יחזקאל would have been hidden away because parts of it seemed to contradict the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Truly, that man is remembered for good, and his name is חנניה בן חזקיה. If not for him, ספר יחזקאל would have been hidden away, because its words contradicted the words of the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to חנניה בן חזקיה, the man whose attic we have been discussing. It tells us about another great thing he did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some details in ספר יחזקאל, mostly about the future בית המקדש and its קרבנות, seem to clash with the laws of the תורה. Because of this, the חכמים wanted to hide the book (גניזה) and keep it out of public use. חנניה is credited with saving it.

keyTerms.meaning: would have been hidden away, put out of use

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
Truly, that man is remembered for good,
and his name is Chananya ben Chizkiya,
for if not for him,
the book of Yechezkel would have been hidden away,
because its words contradicted the words of the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: בְּרַם זָכוּר אוֹתוֹ הָאִישׁ לַטּוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about חנניה בן חזקיה, the man whose attic and group were mentioned earlier
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how a book that seemed to conflict with the תורה stayed part of תנ"ך. Its words were explained, not rejected.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חנניה בן חזקיה prevented ספר יחזקאל from being hidden away.

steps.title: How he did it: three hundred jugs of oil in the attic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא describes what חנניה did. He was given three hundred jugs of oil, sat in his attic, and explained every passage that seemed to contradict the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did he do? They brought up to him three hundred jugs of oil, and he sat in the attic and explained them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how חנניה saved the book and immediately answers. He shut himself in the attic and worked until he had explained all the difficult passages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oil supplied light and food for a long stretch of study without interruption. Through דרשה he resolved each apparent contradiction, so there was no longer any reason to hide the book.

keyTerms.meaning: and he interpreted them (resolved them through explanation)

steps.whatToRemember: חנניה בן חזקיה is praised twice: his group wrote מגילת תענית, and he saved ספר יחזקאל by explaining its difficult passages. Later generations do not record every rescue because there are too many, or because we have become numb to our troubles.

phrases.english: What did he do?

phrases.aramaic: הֶעֱלוּ לוֹ שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת גַּרְבֵי שֶׁמֶן,
phrases.english: They brought up to him three hundred jugs of oil,
and he sat in the attic and interpreted them (the difficult verses).

steps.triggerLanguage: מֶה עָשָׂה? הֶעֱלוּ לוֹ שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת גַּרְבֵי שֶׁמֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the achievement described in step 16 was carried out
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How did חנניה save ספר יחזקאל?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He studied alone in his attic, supplied with three hundred jugs of oil, until he had resolved every contradiction through דרשה.

steps.title: What are the eighteen decrees?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'they decreed eighteen things' and asks which eighteen things these are.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And they decreed eighteen things.' What are these eighteen things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a phrase in the משנה and asks for the details. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that in the attic of חנניה בן חזקיה בן גרון the Sages made eighteen decrees, but it did not list them. The גמרא now wants to know exactly what was decreed. This opens a new section of the סוגיא, after the story of חנניה.

phrases.english: And they decreed eighteen things.
What are these eighteen things?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story of חנניה בן חזקיה and returns to the משנה's mention of the eighteen decrees.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the eighteen decrees mentioned in the משנה.

steps.title: The list of things that disqualify תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by quoting a משנה that lists items the Sages said make תרומה פסולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: These make תרומה unfit: one who eats food with first-level impurity; one who eats food with second-level impurity; one who drinks impure liquids; one whose head and most of his body go into drawn water; a pure person on whose head and most of his body three לוגין of drawn water fell; a ספר תורה; the hands; a טבול יום; and foods and vessels that became impure through liquids.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by bringing a משנה that lists things which disqualify תרומה. These items are among the eighteen decrees; the גמרא names others later in the סוגיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item on the list disqualifies תרומה when it touches it. Some are people (one who ate impure food, a טבול יום), and some are objects or body parts (a ספר תורה, hands, foods and vessels). The גמרא will go through these items one by one in the coming steps, including asking which of them are really rabbinic decrees and which already come from the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Make תרומה unfit (פסול), so it may not be eaten
Drawn water: water drawn in a vessel, not natural spring or rain water
Someone who went to the מקוה today and is not fully pure until nightfall
Plural of לוג, a liquid measure

steps.confusionAlert: 'פוסל' (disqualify) is NOT the same as 'מטמא' (make impure in a way that spreads). Disqualified תרומה cannot be eaten, but it does not pass impurity on to other things. This difference is exactly what the next step is about.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna: these disqualify teruma:
one who eats food of first-degree impurity,
and one who eats food of second-degree impurity,
and one who drinks impure liquids,
and one whose head and most of his body enter drawn water,
and a pure person upon whose head and most of his body fell
three log of drawn water,
and a Torah scroll, and the hands,
and one who immersed that day,
and foods and vessels that became impure through liquids.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18 by quoting a משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The eighteen decrees include the items in the משנה of 'these disqualify תרומה'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This list is the base text for the rest of the סוגיא. Every item on it will be examined to see who taught it and why.

steps.title: Who holds that eating impure food only disqualifies?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that someone who ate first- or second-level impure food disqualifies תרומה, but does not make it fully impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who holds that one who eats food of first-level impurity and one who eats food of second-level impurity disqualify תרומה, but make it impure [they do not]...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts analyzing the first two items on the list. It asks which תנא holds this view; the question continues into the next passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats both eating first-level food and eating second-level food the same: both only disqualify תרומה. The גמרא notices that this is a specific opinion, because one might expect first-level food to give a stronger result than second-level food. So it searches for the תנא behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (which Sage taught this)?
To make impure (in a way that spreads further)

phrases.english: Who is the tanna who holds that

phrases.aramaic: הָאוֹכֵל אוֹכֶל רִאשׁוֹן וְהָאוֹכֵל אוֹכֶל שֵׁנִי —
phrases.english: one who eats first-degree food and one who eats second-degree food —
disqualify, they do disqualify; but render impure...
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud (they do not make it impure).

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תְּנָא הָאוֹכֵל אוֹכֶל רִאשׁוֹן וְהָאוֹכֵל אוֹכֶל שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins examining the first items of the list quoted in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא who holds that eating first- or second-level food only disqualifies תרומה and does not make it impure.
